name: Abdominal Bloating & Distension
description: Feeling of full, tight, or swollen abdomen, often accompanied by visible physical expansion (distension). Driven by gas production from colonic fermentation and altered visceral sensation.
management: Diaphragmatic breathing to relax abdominal wall
red_flags: Inability to pass gas or stool with vomiting

name: Diarrhea-Predominant IBS (IBS-D)
description: Loose, watery stools occurring in >25% of bowel movements, often with urgency and cramping. Caused by accelerated colonic transit, bile acid malabsorption, or osmotic fluid shifts.
dietary_triggers: Excess free fructose & polyols (drawing water into bowel)
red_flags: Nocturnal diarrhea (waking up to pass stool)
Recent antibiotics use (rule out C. diff)

name: Constipation-Predominant IBS (IBS-C)
description: Hard, lumpy, or infrequent stools (<3 per week) occurring in >25% of bowel movements, accompanied by straining and feeling of incomplete evacuation.
non_dietary_triggers: Suppressing urge to defecate due to anxiety or schedule
management: Gradual increase of soluble fiber (Psyllium / Kiwifruit 2 daily)
Osmotic laxatives (Macrogol / PEG 3350) per doctor guidance
red_flags: Rectal bleeding or dark tarry stool

name: Mixed Bowel Habits IBS (IBS-M)
medical_name: IBS with Alternating / Mixed Bowel Habits
description: Alternating between loose/watery stools and hard/straining stools, both occurring in >25% of bowel movements. Requires flexible management strategies.
management: Symptom tracking to isolate specific trigger groups
red_flags: Family history of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)

name: Excessive Gas & Flatulence
description: Passing excessive volume or frequency of intestinal gas, often accompanied by foul odor or lower abdominal discomfort.
management: Soaking dried legumes or choosing canned rinsed legumes
red_flags: Foul odor with involuntary weight loss

name: Abdominal Pain & Cramping
description: Recurrent cramping or dull pain in the lower or mid-abdomen, characteristically related to defecation or changes in stool frequency/form.
dietary_triggers: Large high-fat meals (triggering strong gastrocolic reflex)
non_dietary_triggers: Visceral hypersensitivity (heightened pain sensing in gut nerves)
management: Antispasmodic medication as prescribed by GP
red_flags: Pain that wakes you from sleep
Pain localized strictly in right lower quadrant

name: Nausea & Early Satiety
description: Feeling uncomfortably full shortly after starting a meal, accompanied by mild stomach nausea or upper abdominal heaviness.
dietary_triggers: High-fat fried foods slowing gastric emptying
management: Avoiding lying down for 2 hours post-meal

name: Visceral Hypersensitivity
description: A condition where gut nerves become hyper-reactive, causing normal amounts of gas or intestinal contraction to be perceived as severe pain or pressure.
dietary_triggers: Mechanical wall stretching from osmotic fluid shifts or gas
non_dietary_triggers: Chronic stress, trauma, or sleep deprivation
management: Low-dose neuromodulators (TCAs/SSRIs) as advised by gastroenterologist

name: Postprandial Distress (After-Meal Flare)
description: Sudden urge to pass stool, abdominal pain, or distension within 15-45 minutes after eating a meal.
non_dietary_triggers: Eating on the go / rushing meals
management: Mindful eating: chewing food thoroughly and eating slowly
Splitting daily calories into 4-5 smaller meals

name: Fructan Sensitivity
description: Reaction to fructan polymers found in garlic, onions, wheat, and rye due to absence of human enzymes to break beta-fructose bonds.
dietary_triggers: Garlic, onions, wheat bread, rye, barley, ripe bananas, artichokes
management: Choosing sourdough wheat or gluten-free alternatives
red_flags: Hives, anaphylaxis, breathing difficulty (indicates wheat allergy/coeliac disease, not FODMAP intolerance)

name: Pelvic Floor Dyssynergia
description: Inability to coordinate pelvic floor muscles during defecation, leading to paradoxical contraction instead of relaxation when straining.
red_flags: Complete inability to pass stool for >5 days

name: Gut Microbiome Dysbiosis
description: Imbalance in the diversity or ratio of beneficial vs fermentative commensal gut bacteria, frequently observed post-antibiotics or infection.
dietary_triggers: Overly prolonged restrictive elimination diets (>8 weeks)
management: Specific probiotic strains tested for IBS (e.g., Bifidobacterium infantis 35624)

name: Bile Acid Diarrhea (BAD)
medical_name: Bile Acid Malabsorption / Enterohepatic Circulation Failure
description: Excess bile acids entering the colon, stimulating fluid secretion and rapid motility; often misdiagnosed as IBS-D.
non_dietary_triggers: Ileal resection, gallbladder removal (cholecystectomy), or terminal ileitis
management: Bile acid sequestrants (Colestyramine / Colesevelam) prescribed by doctor
red_flags: Unexplained watery diarrhea after gallbladder surgery

name: Small Intestinal Bacterial Overgrowth (SIBO)
description: Excessive bacterial population in the small intestine fermenting carbohydrates prematurely before colonic transit.
dietary_triggers: Fermentable carbohydrates fermenting early in small bowel
non_dietary_triggers: Anatomic blind loops or low stomach acid
management: Targeted medical antibiotics (e.g., Rifaximin) prescribed by gastroenterologist
Prokinetic support during MMC fasting windows
red_flags: Severe nutritional deficiencies (Vitamin B12, fat-soluble vitamins)

name: Stress & Autonomic Gut Flares
medical_name: Sympathetic Nervous System Activation / Enteric Activation
description: Gut symptom exacerbation triggered directly by stress hormones (cortisol, CRH) altering gut permeability and motility.
dietary_triggers: Caffeine and stimulants during acute stress
non_dietary_triggers: Work burnout, emotional distress, poor sleep quality
red_flags: Suicidal ideation or severe mental health crisis
